text:
Vegas is winless in three, and if you watched the chances you'd shrug. The Golden Knights had 54% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) in those games and lost anyway. That's bad luck, and it's the less interesting part of their season.

The interesting part is how good the process has been under Ryan Craig, hired in June to replace John Tortorella. The Golden Knights are 13-6-4 with 30 points, almost exactly the 29 our expected points say they've earned, and they get 55% of the expected goals overall. Their penalty kill allows just 0.46 expected goals a game. Jack Eichel, Mark Stone and Ivan Barbashev have been the dominant line (59%, 10-4 in goals), and Brayden McNabb with Shea Theodore form the workhorse pair, on for 21 goals for and 13 against in 346 minutes together.

The watch list is short. Victor Olofsson has 11 points in his last ten games against 6.5 expected, a pace well ahead of his chances. Rookie Trevor Connelly has earned more trust, with NHL.com writing he's thriving, and he set up William Karlsson in Tuesday's game against Dallas, per Jesse Granger of The Athletic. The Rasmus Andersson and Jeremy Lauzon pair, outscored 10-5 at 41%, is the weak spot. Our numbers give Vegas 96% playoff odds.
